findings.text: Right-sizing. The decisions are proportionate for a solo MVP: most constants, the H64 choice and the cache were already ratified in the kernel GDD (R-17, X13, KRN-PERF-02 requires O(dirty) encodes), and every verification path is uncached, which keeps the cache low-stakes. The document is about 115 KB, with probe records and vector tables inline, which will make control-manifest extraction and later reads costly. I checked the registry stances: kernel_autoload_or_global, block_as_resource_or_node, write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty, payload_size_check ('never hash input'), the stable-id stance, the control_plane request_restore/request_new_game signatures and presentation_clock 'never hashed'. None contradicts this ADR. ADR-0005 has no registry entries yet (R15).
findings.amendment: Optional: move the probe record (P1 to P16) and the worked vector tables to a companion file such as docs/architecture/adr-0005-vectors.md, or to tests/golden/ with a README, and keep only the decision text and frozen golden values in the ADR. Return the registry candidates now: the restore_epoch state_ownership entry, an api_decision for H64/hash_algo 2, the RngFacet rule and the presentation-RNG stance from T2.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. ADR-0005's Key Interfaces put the pure det code in src/shared/det/, but its § 1.7 row 8 still names src/kernel/det/ for byte writers. ADR-0010 DET-01 and OQ-E repeat src/kernel/det/. ADR-0010 § 1.1 lists only int_math.gd and src/shared/<owner>/. ADR-0010 § 5.4 lists IntMath as trunc_div, floor_div and posmod_i only, while ADR-0005 adds ceil_div, lsr, low32 and the b <= 0 guard.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 decides: src/shared/det/ for all pure det code, and § 1.7 row 8 becomes 'outside src/shared/det/ and tests' (T1). ADR-0010 then amends § 1.1 (adds a src/shared/det/ entry), DET-01 (path), § 5.4 (adds ceil_div, lsr, low32 and the b <= 0 guard returning 0 with a debug assert) and closes OQ-E.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED on all three parts. (a) CanonicalEncoder needs float tokens in src/shared/det/, which SIM-03 bans, and ADR-0005 itself says det_rng_float.gd is the only float file. SIM-04 also bans `float(` and `floor`, which DetRngFloat uses. (b) ADR-0010 § 5.5 says the encoder 'rejects a float in any snapshot', but ADR-0005 § 3.5 rejects floats only in strict mode (tests, STRICT_DEBUG, content hashes); release encodes them normalised. (c) ADR-0010 § 4.1 bounds HashingContext to src/save and src/data, while ADR-0005's Hash64 (src/shared/det) and StateHasher (src/kernel) need it. The IO-01 row does not even list HashingContext.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 (T1) names canonical_encoder.gd and det_rng_float.gd as the two float-allow-listed files and permits HashingContext in hash64.gd and state_hasher.gd. ADR-0010 adds both files to float_allowlist.json (SIM-03) and to a SIM-04 exemption. It rewords § 5.5 to 'the strict-mode encoder (tests and STRICT_DEBUG) rejects a float in a block not on the float allow-list; release encodes normalised'. It rewrites § 4.1 and IO-01 so HashingContext is allowed in src/save, src/data, src/shared/det/hash64.gd and src/kernel/state_hasher.gd.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED for ADR-0005's part. § 1.7 row 2 exempts render-time timers in Adapter/Presenter (TR-pc-027), but SIM-02 has no such exemption. ADR-0005's rule is scoped to sim, kernel and observable presentation files, so it does not itself conflict over created_unix; that part is ADR-0006 against ADR-0010.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 changes the exemption so render-time timers use ADR-0010's injected Clock port, with no Time.* token (T8). ADR-0010 decides the sanctioned wall-clock source for ADR-0006's created_unix, for example a Save/Load-only WallClock port in src/game/ added to the SIM-02 allow-list, and resolves OQ-D.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. ADR-0002 Key Interfaces: request_snapshot() -> void, with the outcome delivered via set_outcome_handler, and ControlOutcome carrying request_kind, outcome, tick and, for a snapshot, the payload deep copy. ADR-0005 Related and ADR-0006 § 3 need the kernel to supply T, state_hash(PERSIST,T) and per-block block_hash/enc_len at capture; ControlOutcome has no such fields. ADR-0002 and the registry use expected_state_hash: int = 0 as 'none', but 0 is a legal H64.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0002 extends the snapshot ControlOutcome with T, state_hash and per-block arrays (block_ids, block_hashes, enc_lens, covering WORLD and PROFILE blocks). It replaces the int sentinel with `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash: int = 0, has_expected_hash: bool = false)` or a verify-mode enum, and updates the registry control_plane signature to match. ADR-0005 adds 'no H64 value is reserved' (T5). ADR-0006 drops its synchronous `-> ControlOutcome{...}` sketch and its Variant/null expected-hash.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED on substance. ADR-0006 § 1.9 rung 1 reuses previous bytes for a block whose cached hash is unchanged and says this 'needs ADR-0004's debug check that every changed block marked a dirty key'. ADR-0005 § 5.4 keeps capture uncached and § 5.2 validates the cache by the touch serial, not by dirty keys. ADR-0004 § 7 says a dirty key cannot serve, because quantised writes mark nothing. ADR-0006 § 1.8 also triggers PROFILE writes from 'ADR-0005's cached block hashes', but capture hashes are uncached. On the naming half, PARTLY REFUTED: ADR-0006 indeed never says block_state_hash, but the Save/Load GDD uses the name 6 times, so ADR-0005 citing SL-16's name is correct and ADR-0006 is the outlier.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0006 rewrites rung 1 as 'skip snapshot() for a block whose ADR-0005 cache entry is valid by touch serial (entry_valid) since the last capture; requires a technical-director ruling on the SAVE-WRK-1 measurement (ADR-0005 OQ-10)' and drops the ADR-0004 dependency. § 1.8 compares the uncached per-block hashes computed at capture. The per-block hash field is named block_state_hash, as in SL-16. ADR-0005 keeps § 5.4 unchanged.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. ADR-0006 defines SaveCodec.hex64_to_int/int_to_hex64 (hex_decode plus a size check, with no lowercase check), duplicating ADR-0005's Hex64. ADR-0005's P16 shows hex_decode accepts uppercase, so ADR-0006 § 1.3's 'lowercase' requirement is not enforced. ADR-0006 § 1.1 line 108 and OQ-I assume the Graph embeds an owner canonical_bytes() as a PackedByteArray snapshot field, which ADR-0005 § 3.1 withdraws: the kernel encodes the Graph's packed-array payload.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0006 deletes SaveCodec's hex helpers and calls Hex64.encode/decode from src/shared/det/ (save may import shared). The 128-bit fields keep a local exact-width check that also validates lowercase. ADR-0006 drops the canonical_bytes() embedding sentence and OQ-I, replacing them with 'the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays; storage is var_to_bytes, hash input is ADR-0005's TLV of the same payload'.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED for ADR-0005's slice. ADR-0001 contains no restore_epoch and no kernel.clock, yet ADR-0005 Depends On attributes the clock view to it. ADR-0003 contains no ModuleFacet.rng, no WriteScope.has_opened, no kernel-owned hashing SnapshotContext (it says one context per kind) and no block_index. ADR-0004's touch_serial is specified in ADR-0004 but is not yet on ADR-0003's H1 allow-list. ADR-0005's Acceptance depends on ADR-0001, 0003 and 0004 being Accepted with these items present.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0003 adds: `ModuleFacet.rng: RngFacet` (null when no streams are declared); `WriteScope.has_opened(block_id)` or a block_index map defined at the freeze; a second SnapshotContext reserved for kernel hash reads, with the re-entrancy flag; kernel.clock view fields (T, world_seed, restore_epoch; restore_epoch non-persisted and non-hashed); and touch_serial plus the hash-cache arrays on the H1 registries allow-list. ADR-0005 fixes its Depends On attribution (T3).

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. architecture.yaml has no entry citing ADR-0005, and ADR-0005 defers its candidates. No existing stance conflicts with ADR-0005 (checked kernel_autoload_or_global, block_as_resource_or_node, write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty, payload_size_check, stable ids, control_plane, presentation_clock). restore_epoch has no state_ownership entry, and three holders are implied: slot_epoch.bin (ADR-0006), the kernel.clock view, and the RngFacet read.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 returns concrete registry candidates for the orchestrator's serialised merge. state_ownership restore_epoch: owner Save/Load (persisted in slot_epoch.bin); the kernel.clock view holds a read-only, non-persisted, non-hashed copy; read only inside RngFacet.draw_epoch. api_decision state_hash: H64 = SHA-256[0:8] LE via HashingContext over ADR-0005 TLV, hash_algo 2. forbidden_pattern presentation_rng: as decided in T2. forbidden_pattern owner_byte_writer.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED for ADR-0005's edges. ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 list each other only under Enables. ADR-0001's Enables omits ADR-0005, although ADR-0005 depends on it. ADR-0007's Depends On omits ADR-0005, although its Validation section says it depends on ADR-0005 for golden vectors. ADR-0005's Enables omits ADR-0013, 0017, 0019, 0024 and 0029, which its own text names.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 adds ADR-0010 to Depends On (layout, allow-lists, lint mechanism), removes it from Enables, and adds 0013, 0017, 0019, 0024 and 0029 to Enables (T9). ADR-0001 adds ADR-0005 to Enables. ADR-0007 adds 'ADR-0005 (golden content-hash vectors only; not an authoring dependency)' to Depends On. ADR-0010 keeps ADR-0005 under Enables only for the DET rule pack.

cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. ADR-0010 OQ-L (a '# nn:' marker form) is stale: ADR-0005 § 1.4 rule 2 adopts ADR-0010's single annotated IntMath.trunc_div site and no marker form. ADR-0009 OQ-F (the cosmetic hash belongs to ADR-0005's family) is answered for the family by ADR-0005 § 2.6 Ihash/h32, but not for the Perception Filter, which ADR-0005 OQ-2 leaves to ADR-0024 (PF D.14 keeps its own masked hash until then).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 closes OQ-L, citing ADR-0005 § 1.4. ADR-0009 closes OQ-F as 'Ihash/Ihash.h32 (ADR-0005 § 2.6) with a fixed non-zero per-system seed; PF D.14 migration is ADR-0024's'. The SIM-12/KRN-04 INPUT_SURFACE allow-list point in R19 is ADR-0010's and does not involve ADR-0005.

cross_adr.text: NEW. ADR-0005 § 2.6 and its Guidelines forbid presentation from calling DetRng.derive, and its Related assumes ADR-0009 agrees. ADR-0009 line 137 explicitly allows 'a truth-channel visual that must match the simulation (a trail) reads rng_derive as the pure function it is'. The Failure & Trail GDD FT-20/AC-134 relies on `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` in presentation (TR-ftrail-044).
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 decides (T2). Recommended: Trail uses Ihash with world_seed as a key; ADR-0009 line 137 changes to 'reads Ihash keyed by world_seed', with a Trail GDD sync for FT-20, D.6 and AC-134. Alternative: allow pure DetRng.derive in presentation for '.vis' names under a lint row, and ADR-0009 keeps its text.

cross_adr.text: NEW. ADR-0004 § 7's MISSED_DIRTY_MARK audit uses ADR-0005's published block_hash(block_id, uncached = true) on every audited block. ADR-0005 § 5.3 returns BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN for any persist == false block, so derived blocks that declare a key space fall outside the audit. ADR-0005 OQ-11 acknowledges this but leaves it open.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0005 resolves OQ-11: in test and STRICT_DEBUG builds the kernel exposes an internal block_hash_any(block_index) (the same path ALL_SIM uses) for ADR-0004's audit and the tripwire. The published block_hash keeps KRN-HASH-03's UNKNOWN rule. ADR-0004 cites the internal read.

findings.text: ADR-0005 contradicts itself on where the determinism code lives and which files may use float tokens and HashingContext. Key Interfaces puts IntMath in src/shared/int_math.gd and DetRng, DetRngFloat, Ihash, Hex64, Hash64 and CanonicalEncoder in src/shared/det/. But § 1.7 row 8 allows encode_s64/encode_u32/encode_double/to_byte_array only 'outside src/kernel/det/', a directory the ADR never creates. That makes the ADR's own CanonicalEncoder and Hex64.encode lint violations. § 2.1 and Key Interfaces call det_rng_float.gd 'the only file with float tokens in src/shared'. CanonicalEncoder, also in src/shared, needs float handling (f != f, f == 0.0, encode_double, binary64 widening of VECTOR2, the strict-mode packed-float scan), so § 1.7 row 3 (SIM-03) bans it too. DetRngFloat also uses `float(` and `floori`, which ADR-0010 SIM-04 bans in src/shared. Hash64.of_bytes (src/shared/det) and StateHasher (src/kernel) use HashingContext, while ADR-0010 § 4.1 limits HashingContext to src/save and src/data. Because these contradictions are inside ADR-0005, not just against a sibling, the ADR cannot be Accepted as written.
findings.amendment: Use one location everywhere: all pure det code goes in src/shared/det/ (IntMath may stay at src/shared/int_math.gd). (1) § 1.7 row 8 reads 'outside src/shared/det/ and tests'. (2) Confine CanonicalEncoder's float handling to one private function, e.g. _encode_float. Put canonical_encoder.gd next to det_rng_float.gd on float_allowlist.json for SIM-03, and exempt both from the SIM-04 `float(`/`floor` bans. Change 'the only file with float tokens' to 'the two allow-listed files'. (3) Add a sentence: HashingContext is permitted in src/shared/det/hash64.gd and src/kernel/state_hasher.gd. (4) Add the matching ADR-0010 amendments to Related (see R5/R6). (5) Optionally, require word boundaries on the § 1.7 tokens (`\bsin\b`, `\bcos\b`, `\bseed\(`, `\bfloat\b`); as listed, they match 'using', 'cost', 'set_world_seed(' and 'float_allowlist'.

findings.text: The ban on presentation RNG conflicts with a GDD requirement that ADR-0005 claims to address. § 2.6, § 2.7, the Guidelines and the Related assumption on ADR-0008/0009 all say presentation 'must never call DetRng.derive'. The Failure & Trail GDD (FT-20, formula at line 572, AC-134) draws `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` in presentation. ADR-0009 § line 137 explicitly allows 'a truth-channel visual that must match the simulation (a trail) reads rng_derive as the pure function it is'. The § 2.7 'Who uses what' table has no Failure & Trail row. The TR table claims TR-ftrail-044 (still marked a Gap in requirements-traceability.md) with a mechanism (posmod_i / int_in on a derive result) that, under the ADR's own rule, presentation may not reach.
findings.amendment: Choose one option and record it. (a) Recommended, because it needs no new lint mechanism: Trail variation becomes `Ihash.h(TRAIL_VIS_SEED, subject_id, stamp_index, world_seed, salt)`, keeping the 'a different world_seed changes a variant' property. Add a GDD sync item for FT-20, D.6 and AC-134 (stub vectors regenerate) and an amendment to ADR-0009 line 137. (b) Alternatively, presentation may call the pure static DetRng.derive for truth-channel visuals under a namespace rule: names end in `.vis`, the key is computed once, never through RngFacet, never a name registered by a SIM module. Add a § 1.7 regex row for it. Either way, add a Failure & Trail row to § 2.7 and rewrite TR-ftrail-044's 'How addressed' cell to name the real mechanism.

findings.text: Right-sizing. The decisions are proportionate for a solo MVP: most constants, the H64 choice and the cache were already ratified in the kernel GDD (R-17, X13, KRN-PERF-02 requires O(dirty) encodes), and every verification path is uncached, which keeps the cache low-stakes. cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED. cross_adr.text: CONFIRMED on substance. ADR-0006 § 1.8 also triggers PROFILE writes from 'ADR-0005's cached block hashes', but capture hashes are uncached. On the naming half, PARTLY REFUTED: ADR-0006 indeed never says block_state_hash, but the Save/Load GDD uses the name 6 times, so ADR-0005 citing SL-16's name is correct and ADR-0006 is the outlier.

The per-block hash field is named block_state_hash, as in SL-16. ADR-0005 keeps § 5.4 unchanged.

findings.text: ADR-0005 contradicts itself on where the determinism code lives and which files may use float tokens and HashingContext. Key Interfaces puts IntMath in src/shared/int_math.gd and DetRng, DetRngFloat, Ihash, Hex64, Hash64 and CanonicalEncoder in src/shared/det/. But § 1.7 row 8 allows encode_s64/encode_u32/encode_double/to_byte_array only 'outside src/kernel/det/', a directory the ADR never creates. That makes the ADR's own CanonicalEncoder and Hex64.encode lint violations. § 2.1 and Key Interfaces call det_rng_float.gd 'the only file with float tokens in src/shared'. CanonicalEncoder, also in src/shared, needs float handling (f != f, f == 0.0, encode_double, binary64 widening of VECTOR2, the strict-mode packed-float scan), so § 1.7 row 3 (SIM-03) bans it too. DetRngFloat also uses `float(` and `floori`, which ADR-0010 SIM-04 bans in src/shared. Hash64.of_bytes (src/shared/det) and StateHasher (src/kernel) use HashingContext, while ADR-0010 § 4.1 limits HashingContext to src/save and src/data. Because these contradictions are inside ADR-0005, not just against a sibling, the ADR cannot be Accepted as written.
findings.amendment: Use one location everywhere: all pure det code goes in src/shared/det/ (IntMath may stay at src/shared/int_math.gd). (1) § 1.7 row 8 reads 'outside src/shared/det/ and tests'. (2) Confine CanonicalEncoder's float handling to one private function, e.g. _encode_float. Put canonical_encoder.gd next to det_rng_float.gd on float_allowlist.json for SIM-03, and exempt both from the SIM-04 `float(`/`floor` bans. Change 'the only file with float tokens' to 'the two allow-listed files'. (3) Add a sentence: HashingContext is permitted in src/shared/det/hash64.gd and src/kernel/state_hasher.gd. (4) Add the matching ADR-0010 amendments to Related (see R5/R6). (5) Optionally, require word boundaries on the § 1.7 tokens (`\bsin\b`, `\bcos\b`, `\bseed\(`, `\bfloat\b`); as listed, they match 'using', 'cost', 'set_world_seed(' and 'float_allowlist'.

findings.text: The ban on presentation RNG conflicts with a GDD requirement that ADR-0005 claims to address. § 2.6, § 2.7, the Guidelines and the Related assumption on ADR-0008/0009 all say presentation 'must never call DetRng.derive'. The Failure & Trail GDD (FT-20, formula at line 572, AC-134) draws `rng_derive(world_seed, "trail.vis", (subject_id << 20) | stamp_index)` in presentation. ADR-0009 § line 137 explicitly allows 'a truth-channel visual that must match the simulation (a trail) reads rng_derive as the pure function it is'. The § 2.7 'Who uses what' table has no Failure & Trail row. The TR table claims TR-ftrail-044 (still marked a Gap in requirements-traceability.md) with a mechanism (posmod_i / int_in on a derive result) that, under the ADR's own rule, presentation may not reach.
findings.amendment: Choose one option and record it. (a) Recommended, because it needs no new lint mechanism: Trail variation becomes `Ihash.h(TRAIL_VIS_SEED, subject_id, stamp_index, world_seed, salt)`, keeping the 'a different world_seed changes a variant' property. Add a GDD sync item for FT-20, D.6 and AC-134 (stub vectors regenerate) and an amendment to ADR-0009 line 137. (b) Alternatively, presentation may call the pure static DetRng.derive for truth-channel visuals under a namespace rule: names end in `.vis`, the key is computed once, never through RngFacet, never a name registered by a SIM module. Add a § 1.7 regex row for it. Either way, add a Failure & Trail row to § 2.7 and rewrite TR-ftrail-044's 'How addressed' cell to name the real mechanism.

findings.text: Amendments to ADR-0001 and ADR-0003 are unapplied, and one is attributed to the wrong ADR. Depends On says ADR-0001 'the kernel clock carries T, world_seed and restore_epoch', but ADR-0001 never mentions restore_epoch or kernel.clock. The clock read view comes from kernel GDD CR-8, ADR-0006 § 3.5 and ADR-0003's views. Neither ADR-0001 nor ADR-0003 contains ModuleFacet.rng, WriteScope.has_opened, or a kernel-owned SnapshotContext for block_hash reads outside SAVING. ADR-0003 says 'the MVP needs one context per kind'. ADR-0005's own Acceptance condition is that ADR-0001/0003/0004 are Accepted, so these must land first. ADR-0003 also identifies blocks by `open_for(block_id: StringName)`, while ADR-0005 uses `has_opened(block_index: int)`, `touch_serial(block_index)` and cache arrays indexed by an undefined block_index.
findings.amendment: Rewrite the Depends On cell: ADR-0003 owns ModuleFacet.rng, WriteScope.has_opened, the kernel.clock view fields (T, world_seed, restore_epoch; the restore_epoch field is non-persisted) and a second SnapshotContext instance that the kernel uses for hash reads. ADR-0001 is cited only for injection and no-global. List these items under Related as 'cross-ADR amendments required before Accept'. Define block_index once: the dense index assigned at the registry freeze in ascending block_id code-point order, never persisted or hashed. Either make has_opened take block_id, or state the id-to-index map.

findings.text: The Acceptance gate is ambiguous and may deadlock. The Ordering Note says Acceptance 'also requires S0-a to S0-d on a release export and the cross-OS golden job'. § 6 defines that job as comparing graph_state_hash_*.txt Graph fixture files, which need Graph code (ADR-0011/0012). docs/CLAUDE.md auto-blocks stories that reference a Proposed ADR, so the Graph code cannot be written until this ADR is Accepted. macOS sits in the gate even though OQ-5 doubts it is a target. Migration Plan item 8 says S0-e and the cross-OS job will be added to architecture.md's spike table, but architecture.md has neither (grep for S0-e and 'cross-OS' finds nothing). So a gate exists here that the project plan does not show.
findings.amendment: Gate Acceptance on: S0-a to S0-d as scratch scripts on a template_release export (Windows plus Linux/Deck); S0-e with the synthetic stand-ins § 1 already names; and the § 2.4, § 2.6, § 3.7 and § 4.5 vectors reproducing on Windows and Linux CI. Move the Graph golden files (TR-lsg-031) to Validation Criteria for the Graph epic. Mark the macOS leg advisory until a target decision is made. Add S0-e and the cross-OS vector job to architecture.md § Spikes, with the user's approval, before this ADR is Accepted.

I checked the registry stances: kernel_autoload_or_global, block_as_resource_or_node, write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty, payload_size_check ('never hash input'), the stable-id stance, the control_plane request_restore/request_new_game signatures and presentation_clock 'never hashed'. None contradicts this ADR. ADR-0005 has no registry entries yet (R15).
findings.amendment: Optional: move the probe record (P1 to P16) and the worked vector tables to a companion file such as docs/architecture/adr-0005-vectors.md, or to tests/golden/ with a README, and keep only the decision text and frozen golden values in the ADR.
